profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the modeling lead and the evaluation/infrastructure lead for an ML research project reproducing and extending a paper on multi-modal neurological image fusion with a wavelet-pooled edge-preserving autoencoder. The team is preparing an internal milestone for a lab demo next week: the modeling side will hand off a trained checkpoint and inference outputs, while the evaluation side will run the standardized comparison notebook and assemble figures/tables for the demo deck. The agenda is to align on the checkpoint handoff, what counts as the 'validation run,' where the shared artifacts will live, and what exactly should be included in the demo-ready result bundle. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on interfaces, file locations, and status for the handoff, even though some second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Dr. Nisha Raman
members.expertise: Medical image fusion, representation learning, unsupervised training pipelines, neuroimaging preprocessing
members.background: Nisha leads the implementation of the wavelet pooled edge-preserving autoencoder and previously worked on MRI-PET registration and image enhancement in an academic medical imaging lab.
members.private_state: She wants the handoff to look stable enough for the demo without reopening model-side work, is trying to avoid another retraining cycle, and is concerned that evaluation may use an older preprocessing path that makes the model look inconsistent.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'latest checkpoint,' they mean the most recently promoted run that passed her internal sanity checks, not literally the newest file produced by training.

A 'validation run' for this project means inference on the small curated sanity subset of registered neuro cases used during development, because that is the only set with quickly inspectable overlays.
The shared 'results bundle' naturally includes fused images, a metrics CSV, and the exact preprocessing manifest used to generate them, because otherwise results are not reproducible.
Anything placed in the team's shared experiment folder can be treated as the current artifact of record unless someone explicitly says it is archival.

members.name: Evan Morales
members.role: Research Engineer, Evaluation and Infrastructure Lead
members.expertise: Experiment tracking, evaluation automation, reproducible ML pipelines, benchmark reporting
members.background: Evan maintains the lab's standardized benchmarking notebooks and artifact storage conventions, and previously supported several multimodal vision projects moving from exploratory code to reusable evaluation pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the evaluation pipeline uniform across projects, minimize bespoke exceptions, and get a clean package ready for the demo deck without having to chase missing files at the last minute.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says 'latest checkpoint,' they mean the chronologically newest model artifact in the experiment tracker for the current branch, because that is what automation resolves by default.
A 'validation run' means running the standard held-out evaluation split through the benchmark notebook, even if only summary metrics are inspected before the demo.

A 'results bundle' for coordination purposes means only the outputs consumed by downstream reporting: fused PNGs, final summary table, and the selected checkpoint reference, not intermediate manifests.
The artifact of record is whatever is registered in the evaluation store under the milestone tag; ad hoc team folders are useful for transfer but not authoritative.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the 'latest checkpoint' for the handoff and demo run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the most recent checkpoint she has manually promoted after sanity-checking fusion quality on the curated neuro subset (run wp_epae_042, epoch 68).
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the most recently generated checkpoint in the tracker for that training line, which automation will resolve to the newest saved artifact (run wp_epae_042, epoch 72).
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research teams, 'latest checkpoint' is a routine shorthand that usually passes without elaboration, and both believe the difference between newest and promoted newest is already obvious from normal workflow.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether the model is 'validated' and say the evaluation side can run the 'validation set' before the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks validated means the model has passed qualitative and quantitative checks on a 24-pair curated registered sanity subset covering MRI-CT and MRI-PET examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks validated means the model has been run on the formal held-out benchmark split of 120 pairs through the lab's standard notebook and produced the summary metrics table.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same project-management language around validation, but each assumes the other's criterion is the established lab norm; the conversation is about coordination, so neither expects to renegotiate what validation means.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nisha will send over the 'results bundle' for Evan to plug into the demo notebook.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes fused NIfTI volumes, representative PNG panels, metrics CSVs, and the preprocessing manifest with registration/cropping metadata for each pair.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects only the downstream-ready items: selected fused PNG exports, one summary CSV, and a checkpoint pointer; he does not expect manifests or volumetric intermediates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds operationally specific enough to both of them, and each assumes the omitted details are simply standard packaging conventions from their own workstream.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to putting everything in the 'shared folder' and being able to pull from there for the milestone.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the lab's shared project drive folder /neurofusion/demo_ready/ is the current source of truth once she uploads the handoff there.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the experiment artifacts become official only after they are mirrored into the evaluation store and tagged milestone_demo_v1; the shared drive is just a transfer location.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both frequently use both storage systems, and in casual coordination talk 'shared folder' sounds like a harmless logistics reference rather than a statement about record ownership.
